fact: The World Bank's Additional Financing for the Social Protection and Economic Resilience Project (US$154.4m, estimated board date 28 May 2026) funds the legal and technical establishment of Mozambique's National Social Registry and its interoperability with civil registration, health and education data systems.

INGD's digital registry of humanitarian-assistance beneficiaries is being tested in Beira and is due nationwide in October 2026, and its director of prevention says it should interoperate with the INAS database to show who has already received assistance.

Mozambique's disaster agency INGD says its WFP-funded Beneficiary and Humanitarian Assistance Management System (SGBAH), in field pilot and validated ahead of an October 2026 national launch, will be interoperable with the database of the social action institute INAS, which runs support programmes for vulnerable households.
system: Beneficiary and Humanitarian Assistance Management System (SGBAH)
